pk.context: 150 mg intramuscular, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: sterile aqueous suspension in a vial

tell: A progesterone derivative given every 3 months by deep intramuscular injection, with a boxed warning for bone loss.

clues.text: It is 86% bound to plasma proteins, mainly serum albumin, and not to sex hormone-binding globulin. It is extensively metabolized in the liver, and its metabolites are excreted in urine mostly as glucuronide conjugates.
An acetate ester of a progesterone derivative; the parent steroid has a molecular weight of 344.5. An odorless crystalline powder, insoluble in water.
Marketed under an NDA, supplied as vials and prefilled syringes, and given as a single injection every 3 months.

Boxed warning for bone mineral density loss; contraindicated with thromboembolic disorders, breast malignancy, significant liver disease or undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Chest pain and injection site pain are reported.
Prevention of pregnancy in females of reproductive potential, though not recommended as a long-term method beyond 2 years.
Inhibits the secretion of gonadotropins, mainly preventing follicular maturation and ovulation, and thickens cervical mucus.
The generic name begins with M and has twenty-six letters in two words.
